pattern.description: A white website nav bar (logo, Software, Pricing, Resources) drops in from the top while the hero wordmark, headline and side decorations scale up together and resettle below it, turning a logo card into a homepage hero layout.
pattern.why_premium: The title card changes into the real product website in one move, with no cut, so the brand intro leads straight into the product context. Every layer moves on the same ease, so the reframe reads as a single camera-like gesture.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline at t0: gsap.fromTo('.nav', {yPercent:-100}, {yPercent:0, duration:0.3, ease:'power3.out'}); nav children ride with the bar (optional stagger 0.02). Same start: gsap.fromTo('.hero-group', {scale:0.92, y:-20}, {scale:1, y:0, duration:0.4, ease:'power2.out', transformOrigin:'50% 40%'}); sparkles gsap.to('.sparkle', {opacity:0, scale:0.6, duration:0.25, ease:'power2.in'}).
build_hint.remotion: const p = interpolate(frame,[0,8],[0,1],{easing:Easing.out(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight:'clamp'}); nav translateY = (1-p)*-110px; hero group scale = interpolate(frame,[0,10],[0.92,1],{easing:Easing.out(Easing.quad)}). Sparkle opacity 1 to 0 over 6 frames with Easing.in(Easing.quad). No spring (no overshoot visible).

notes: b01 is a diff union (top 47% of frame) rather than a tight nav-bar box; it stands for the white nav bar. The hero scale-up could be a slight camera push but camera.move is none, so it is treated as a layout change. Sparkle sub-boxes b12/b13 belong to the same sparkle group as b11.
